title: Mayank Agarwal Joins Ben Stokes' Durham for County Championship Push
excerpt: The India opener signed a four-game Division Two contract to replace David Bedingham as Durham chase promotion.
body:
• Mayank Agarwal has signed a four-game County Championship Division Two contract with Durham
  • He replaces David Bedingham and joins a squad containing England captain Ben Stokes
  • Durham are leading Division Two and seeking promotion to the top flight
  • Agarwal has 1,488 Test runs from 21 Tests, including four centuries and a career-best 243

India opener Mayank Agarwal has signed a four-game County Championship Division Two contract with Durham, joining a squad headlined by England Test captain Ben Stokes as the club pushes for promotion.

The Deal

Agarwal replaces David Bedingham in Durham's overseas player slot. The 35-year-old arrives with strong credentials in English conditions: he scored 201 runs during a stint with Yorkshire in 2025, including a knock of 175 against Durham themselves, according to NDTV Sports.

Durham are currently leading Division Two and have their sights set on a return to the County Championship's top tier. The addition of an experienced international batter for the final stretch of the season signals the club's ambition to secure promotion.

International Pedigree

Agarwal has played 21 Tests for India, accumulating 1,488 runs at an average that includes four centuries. His career-best score of 243, made against Bangladesh in 2019, remains one of the highest by an Indian opener in Test cricket. He also has a double century against South Africa to his name.

While Agarwal has been on the fringes of India's Test setup in recent years, his domestic record remains prolific. His ability to occupy the crease and score heavily in English conditions made him an attractive option for Durham's promotion push.

A Growing Trend

Agarwal's signing is the latest in a growing trend of Indian cricketers gaining experience in county cricket. Auqib Nabi recently joined Surrey for three county games ahead of India's Test series against New Zealand. The Indian cricket board has become more open to allowing players to play county cricket as preparation for overseas Test assignments.

For Durham, the combination of Stokes and Agarwal provides significant international experience in the batting lineup during the most critical phase of their promotion campaign. The club's remaining four matches will determine whether they return to Division One.
